claims.claim: Binance published an incident update and described its root-cause account as an initial investigation.
claims.boundary: This supports that Binance made the statement; it does not independently establish the root cause.
claims.closure_test: Replace preliminary wording only after a dated technical post-mortem with reproducible incident evidence is captured.

claims.claim: The reviewed sources report incident-scale estimates near USD 6.3 billion, but the exact figures and chain inclusion rules remain source-specific.
claims.speaker_attribution: Binance: around USD 6.3B impact; TRM: USD 6.36B across ten chains; Bitquery: USD 6.3B across nine chains at theft-time prices.
counter_evidence: BSEC-S004 reports a different USD 5.3B Glassnode figure in a syndicated article.
claims.boundary: Impact, stolen value and attacker holdings are not interchangeable. Values depend on chain set, token set, price time and attribution rule.
claims.closure_test: Reconcile every included transfer to a public transaction, declared price timestamp and stable chain-inclusion rule.

claims.claim: The amount frozen is not yet a single reconciled number in this packet.
claims.speaker_attribution: Binance: approximately USD 3B frozen; TRM and Bitquery: approximately USD 2.7B independently matched under their methods.
counter_evidence: The sources use different cutoffs and definitions; some include issuer freezes and Arbitrum rescue while media reports may repeat earlier estimates.
claims.boundary: Frozen does not mean recovered, returned, compensated or permanently unavailable to an attacker.
claims.closure_test: Produce a transaction-level freeze ledger with asset, amount, chain, authority, timestamp, current status and double-count controls.

claims.claim: Binance promised to cover all losses from SAFU and company funds.
claims.boundary: A compensation promise is not evidence of completed compensation, final loss size, source-of-funds execution or user-level restoration.
claims.closure_test: Capture dated completion evidence and reconcile compensated amounts to eligible losses without counting frozen or recovered assets twice.

claims.claim: Binance said a compromised DevOps laptop may have enabled unauthorized withdrawals and said it had found no evidence of a wallet private-key leak.
counter_evidence: A valid on-chain signature shows authorization at the chain layer; it cannot identify the off-chain requester or exclude every key-compromise scenario.
claims.boundary: Chain data can be compatible with the operator account but cannot independently establish the laptop compromise or prove a negative about key leakage.
claims.closure_test: Capture the technical post-mortem, affected trust boundaries, key custody evidence, audit logs and an independently reviewable chronology.

claims.claim: Ethereum recorded a successful transaction at 2026-10-29T20:24:23Z from 0x7c86…b5ca0 to 0x28c6…d60 in block 26300770; the receipt status is success and contains 64 logs.
claims.boundary: This verifies the transaction object, execution receipt and block timestamp only. It does not by itself establish wallet ownership, total stolen value, root cause or attribution.
claims.closure_test: No closure required for the recorded object; any interpretation must separately prove address labels and decode transfers.

claims.claim: TRM attributes the incident to TraderTraitor / North Korea with high confidence.
counter_evidence: Binance named no actor in the captured notice; Bitquery states that the chain does not show who requested the signatures.
claims.boundary: Behavioral similarity, funding patterns and undisclosed intelligence are analytic inputs, not independently reproduced attribution in this packet.
claims.closure_test: Require attributable primary evidence or multiple independently reviewable intelligence disclosures that expose the reasoning and rule out material alternatives.

claims.claim: The reviewed analytics disagree on whether the incident set spans nine or ten chains.
counter_evidence: TRM includes Avalanche; the reviewed Bitquery count lists nine chains and treats some links as inference from timing, construction and Binance totals.
claims.boundary: A shared headline total can conceal different inclusion rules.
claims.closure_test: Publish a chain-by-chain inclusion matrix with transaction identifiers, address-label basis and explicit reasons for including inferred clusters.

claims.claim: The public packet does not establish post-incident reserve coverage, liability coverage, compensation completion or solvency.
counter_evidence: Binance states that user funds are safe and promises an updated proof of reserves, but the promised update was not available by the cutoff.
claims.boundary: Proof of reserves is point-in-time and does not alone establish all liabilities, liquidity, loss absorption, off-chain obligations or solvency.
claims.closure_test: Obtain the original pre-incident snapshot and address bundle, an explicit post-remediation snapshot, liability methodology, incident adjustments and independently reproducible reconciliation.

claims.claim: A dated Eastmoney page syndicated from 财联社 reported market reaction and repeated differing incident and freeze estimates.
counter_evidence: Its USD 5.3B figure differs from the operator and two analytics; its underlying Glassnode material was not captured as an original source.
claims.boundary: This supports what the media page reported, not the truth of each repeated figure or any causal market claim.
claims.closure_test: Capture each underlying original source and align timestamps before using its figures as event evidence.
